Egypt has received nearly $90 billion in cumulative US bilateral aid since 1946 and, alongside Israel, was specifically exempted from President Trump's 2025 global foreign-aid pause; the FY2026 NDAA separately authorizes new US defense assistance along Egypt's border with Sudan. Egypt controls the Suez Canal, one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints, reinforcing its enduring strategic importance to Washington

The US suspended all foreign aid to Afghanistan in February 2025 under Executive Order 14169, cutting off an estimated $1.7 billion for the year; the move caused roughly 50 aid organizations to partly or wholly suspend operations, deepening a humanitarian crisis under Taliban rule, which the US and most other governments still do not formally recognize

The US and Uzbekistan signed a 'Joint Investment Framework' in February 2026 through the US International Development Finance Corp, prioritizing US investment in Uzbekistan's exploration, extraction, and processing of critical minerals like tungsten, copper, and uranium, and proposing a new US-Uzbekistan Joint Investment Holding Company; the deal followed a November 2025 White House summit where Trump hosted the leaders of all five Central Asian states

Oman has served as the essential mediator between the US and Yemen's Houthi movement for years, brokering a May 6, 2025 ceasefire that ended the US-UK bombing campaign in Yemen after the Houthis agreed to stop attacking US vessels; Oman also facilitated the release of the Galaxy Leader crew and has hosted broader US-Iran nuclear talks, even as its territory has reportedly been used as a smuggling conduit for weapons reaching the Houthis.
